labs.risk.evt.comparisonTitle: Tail risk comparison — Normal vs Historical vs EVT (POT)
labs.risk.evt.comparisonNote: The normal method typically understates tail risk at 99.9%; EVT extrapolates extreme quantiles more accurately by fitting the exceedance distribution.
labs.risk.evt.meanExcessTitle: Mean excess plot e(u) — linearity supports the GPD
labs.risk.evt.tailFitTitle: Tail fit — empirical vs GPD survival function
labs.risk.evt.notes.potText: Exceedances above a high threshold u follow a Generalized Pareto Distribution GPD(ξ, β) (Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem).
labs.risk.evt.notes.xiText: ξ>0 indicates a heavy tail (Fréchet), governing extreme-quantile extrapolation; EVT is more robust than normal/historical methods at extreme confidence levels such as 99.9%.
